answer: In an ocean of AI agents, voting power comes from funds locked in escrow, not the number of accounts. An attacker can create a thousand identities and let them wander across markets, but splitting a deposit among them adds no voting power. To gain more influence, the attacker must lock more capital for the full voting period, losing liquidity and other returns. Trust rests on a measurable cost rather than an ivory tower claim that each account is unique.
